name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q01 - Scientists and their cellular discoveries

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists in the first list with their corresponding discoveries in the second list and select the correct combination.

List IList II
A. Anton Von Leeuwenhoek(i) Discovered the nucleus
B. Robert Brown(ii) First observed ribosomes as dense particles
C. Camillo Golgi(iii) First saw and described a live cell
D. George Palade(iv) Observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Key milestones in cell biology were established through microscopic observations of live cells and intracellular organelles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Scientist and Discovery
Anton Von Leeuwenhoek was the first to see and describe a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus in 1831. Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus, which were later named Golgi bodies. George Palade (1953) first observed ribosomes under the electron microscope as dense granular particles.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Anton Von Leeuwenhoek with first describing a live cell, Robert Brown with discovering the nucleus, Camillo Golgi with observing reticular structures near the nucleus, and George Palade with first observing ribosomes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q02 - Four basic shapes of bacteria

questiontext.text:
Match the bacterial categories with their characteristic shapes and select the correct option.

List IList II
A. Bacillus(i) Comma-shaped
B. Coccus(ii) Rod-like
C. Vibrio(iii) Spiral
D. Spirillum(iv) Spherical

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prokaryotic bacterial cells exhibit four basic morphological shapes despite having a fundamentally similar cellular organisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Bacterial Shape
Bacillus bacteria are rod-like in shape. Coccus bacteria are spherical. Vibrio bacteria are comma-shaped. Spirillum bacteria are spiral in shape.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate pairings are Bacillus with rod-like, Coccus with spherical, Vibrio with comma-shaped, and Spirillum with spiral.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q03 - Types of plastids and stored nutrients

questiontext.text:
Match the types of plastids with their respective stored nutrients or pigments.

List IList II
A. Amyloplasts(i) Store oils and fats
B. Elaioplasts(ii) Contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments
C. Aleuroplasts(iii) Store carbohydrates (starch)
D. Chromoplasts(iv) Store proteins

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plastids in plant cells are classified into chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and colourless leucoplasts based on their pigments and storage functions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Plastid Type
Among leucoplasts, amyloplasts store carbohydrates such as starch (for example, in potato), elaioplasts store oils and fats, and aleuroplasts store proteins. Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls, imparting yellow, orange, or red colour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Amyloplasts with storing carbohydrates (starch), Elaioplasts with storing oils and fats, Aleuroplasts with storing proteins, and Chromoplasts with containing fat-soluble carotenoid pigments.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q04 - Endomembrane system organelles and functions

questiontext.text:
Match the components of the endomembrane system with their primary cellular functions.

List IList II
A. Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum(i) Formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids
B. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum(ii) Protein synthesis and secretion
C. Golgi apparatus(iii) Digestion of macromolecules at acidic pH
D. Lysosomes(iv) Synthesis of lipids and steroidal hormones

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The endomembrane system comprises organelles whose functions are coordinated: the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Organelle Function
Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) bears ribosomes on its surface and is active in protein synthesis and secretion. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks ribosomes and is the major site for lipid synthesis, including steroidal hormones in animal cells. The Golgi apparatus packages materials and is an important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. Lysosomes are rich in hydrolytic enzymes optimally active at acidic pH for digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum with protein synthesis and secretion, Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum with synthesis of lipids and steroidal hormones, Golgi apparatus with formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids, and Lysosomes with digestion of macromolecules at acidic pH.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q05 - Prokaryotic structures and their roles

questiontext.text:
Match the prokaryotic structures with their characteristic features or functions.

List IList II
A. Mesosome(i) Small circular DNA conferring antibiotic resistance
B. Plasmid(ii) Inclusion body found in photosynthetic bacteria
C. Fimbriae(iii) Plasma membrane infoldings aiding DNA replication
D. Gas vacuole(iv) Bristle-like fibres helping attach to host tissues

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prokaryotic cells possess specialised membranous extensions, extrachromosomal DNA, surface appendages, and non-membranous inclusion bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Prokaryotic Structure
Mesosomes are specialised infoldings of the plasma membrane (vesicles, tubules, and lamellae) that help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells. Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules outside the genomic DNA that confer unique phenotypic characters such as antibiotic resistance. Fimbriae are small bristle-like fibres sprouting from the cell that help bacteria attach to rocks in streams and host tissues. Gas vacuoles are inclusion bodies found in blue-green, purple, and green photosynthetic bacteria.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate pairings are Mesosome with plasma membrane infoldings aiding DNA replication, Plasmid with small circular DNA conferring antibiotic resistance, Fimbriae with bristle-like fibres helping attach to host tissues, and Gas vacuole with inclusion body found in photosynthetic bacteria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q06 - Eukaryotic organelle membranes and sub-structures

questiontext.text:
Match the eukaryotic sub-structures with the organelles in which they are found.

List IList II
A. Cristae(i) Flattened membranous sacs in chloroplast stroma
B. Cisternae(ii) Infoldings of inner mitochondrial membrane
C. Thylakoids(iii) Single membrane bounding the plant vacuole
D. Tonoplast(iv) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Eukaryotic cells display extensive compartmentalisation through distinct membrane-bound organelles, each possessing characteristic internal structures.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Sub-structure
Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane towards the matrix. Cisternae are flat, disc-shaped sacs (0.5 to 1.0 micrometre diameter) stacked parallel to each other in the Golgi apparatus. Thylakoids are organised flattened membranous sacs present in the stroma of chloroplasts. Tonoplast is the single membrane that bounds the vacuole.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Cristae with infoldings of inner mitochondrial membrane, Cisternae with disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus, Thylakoids with flattened membranous sacs in chloroplast stroma, and Tonoplast with single membrane bounding the plant vacuole.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q07 - Cell wall components and membrane transport

questiontext.text:
Match the cellular structures and transport processes with their accurate biochemical or functional descriptions.

List IList II
A. Middle lamella(i) Cytoplasmic connections between neighbouring plant cells
B. Plasmodesmata(ii) Energy-dependent transport against concentration gradient
C. Algal cell wall(iii) Layer mainly of calcium pectate gluing adjacent cells
D. Active transport(iv) Composed of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant and algal cells are surrounded by a rigid cell wall and interconnected by specialised junctions, while plasma membranes regulate molecular transport across concentration gradients.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Term
The middle lamella is a layer composed mainly of calcium pectate that holds or glues neighbouring plant cells together. Plasmodesmata traverse the cell wall and middle lamellae to connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells. The algal cell wall consists of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate. Active transport is an ATP-utilising, energy-dependent process that moves ions or molecules from lower to higher concentration against their concentration gradient (such as the sodium-potassium pump).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Middle lamella with layer mainly of calcium pectate gluing adjacent cells, Plasmodesmata with cytoplasmic connections between neighbouring plant cells, Algal cell wall with composed of cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals, and Active transport with energy-dependent transport against concentration gradient.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q08 - Ribosome subunits, axoneme, and centriole organisation

questiontext.text:
Match the non-membrane-bound structures and microtubule assemblies with their structural specifications.

List IList II
A. 80S ribosome(i) Core of cilium with 9+2 microtubule array
B. 70S ribosome(ii) Composed of 60S and 40S subunits
C. Axoneme(iii) Cartwheel organisation with nine peripheral tubulin triplets
D. Centriole(iv) Composed of 50S and 30S subunits

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ribosomes are classified by their sedimentation coefficients (Svedberg's unit), while eukaryotic locomotory organelles and centrosomes are built from distinct microtubule arrangements.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Structure
Eukaryotic cytoplasmic 80S ribosomes consist of 60S and 40S subunits. Prokaryotic, mitochondrial, and chloroplast 70S ribosomes consist of 50S and 30S subunits. The axoneme is the core of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum, exhibiting a 9+2 array (nine peripheral microtubule doublets and a central pair). A centriole displays a cartwheel organisation made of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, where each fibril is a triplet connected to a central proteinaceous hub via radial spokes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The accurate pairings are 80S ribosome with composed of 60S and 40S subunits, 70S ribosome with composed of 50S and 30S subunits, Axoneme with core of cilium with 9+2 microtubule array, and Centriole with cartwheel organisation with nine peripheral tubulin triplets.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELLTHEUNITOFLIFE_MCQ_Q09 - Nuclear components and chromosome structures

questiontext.text:
Match the nuclear and chromosomal components with their correct structural or functional descriptions.

List IList II
A. Chromatin(i) Small fragment formed by non-staining secondary constriction
B. Kinetochore(ii) Disc-shaped structure on sides of the centromere
C. Satellite(iii) Passage for bidirectional movement of RNA and proteins
D. Nuclear pore(iv) Nucleoprotein fibres containing DNA, histones, and RNA

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The interphase nucleus contains chromatin and nuclear pores in the nuclear envelope, while dividing cells display condensed chromosomes with centromeres, kinetochores, and occasionally satellites.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Component
Chromatin consists of nucleoprotein fibres containing DNA, basic histone proteins, non-histone proteins, and RNA. Every chromosome has a primary constriction (centromere) on the sides of which disc-shaped structures called kinetochores are present. A satellite is a small fragment-like appearance formed when a chromosome has a non-staining secondary constriction at a constant location. Nuclear pores are minute interruptions formed by the fusion of the two nuclear envelope membranes, serving as passages for bidirectional movement of RNA and protein molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct biological pairings are Chromatin with nucleoprotein fibres containing DNA, histones, and RNA, Kinetochore with disc-shaped structure on sides of the centromere, Satellite with small fragment formed by non-staining secondary constriction, and Nuclear pore with passage for bidirectional movement of RNA and proteins.
